name: Remembering the Lord at the hour of death
method_summary: BhG 8.5–7 (with 7.30, 8.10, 8.13): whoever leaves the body at the end remembering the Lord alone attains his state; since one goes to whatever state one remembers at the end, having always been shaped by it, the Lord is to be remembered at all times; at departure the yogin with steady mind and devotion reaches the supreme divine Person, or, uttering Oṃ and remembering him, the supreme goal.
prerequisites: lifelong remembrance, having 'always been shaped' by the state remembered (8.6–7)
knowing the Lord with adhibhūta, adhidaiva and adhiyajña (7.30)

warnings.text: Whatever state one remembers when leaving the body, to that one goes (so the remembrance must be cultivated at all times).

name: Constant remembrance of the Lord (smaraṇa)
method_summary: BhG 8.7–8, 8.14; 9.22, 9.34: remember the Lord at all times while doing one's duty ('remember me and fight'); with a mind yoked by the yoga of repeated practice (abhyāsa-yoga), going nowhere else, continually contemplate the supreme Person; remember him constantly, day after day, with mind on nothing else — for such an ever-yoked yogin he is easy to reach; think of him with no other; 'be one whose mind is on me'.
signs_of_progress: the Lord becomes 'easy to attain' (sulabha) for the constantly remembering yogin (8.14)

name: Yogic departure at death
method_summary: Summary of the Gītā's account only: at the time of departure, with unmoving mind, devotion and the power of yoga, the breath is settled between the brows (8.10); the gates (of the senses) are restrained, the mind confined in the heart, the breath placed in the head, and, established in yogic concentration (yoga-dhāraṇā), one utters Oṃ, remembers the Lord and leaves the body, going to the supreme goal (8.12–13). The Gītā gives no further method.
prerequisites: a mind trained by repeated practice (8.8)

name: Fixing the gaze or breath between the eyebrows (bhrū-madhya)
method_summary: BhG 8.10: at the time of departure the yogin, with steady mind, devotion and the power of yoga, makes the breath (prāṇa) enter fully between the brows and so reaches the supreme divine Person.

name: Undivided devotion (ananya-bhakti)
method_summary: BhG 7–9: worship of the Lord with mind on nothing else — the knower 'devoted to the One' (eka-bhakti, 7.17); constant remembrance with undivided mind (8.14); the supreme Person is attainable by undivided devotion (8.22); the great souls worship him with undistracted mind, knowing him as the imperishable origin of beings (9.13); for those who think of him with no other and worship him he carries gain and security (9.22); even one of very bad conduct who worships him with undivided devotion is to be deemed good, having resolved rightly (9.30); summed up in 9.34: mind on him, devoted to him, sacrificing to him, bowing to him, with him as the supreme aim.
signs_of_progress: quickly becomes righteous (dharmātman) and attains lasting peace (9.31)
the Lord bears his gain and security (9.22)

name: Taking refuge in the Lord alone (śaraṇāgati)
method_summary: BhG 7.14, 7.19, 7.29; 9.32: those who take refuge in the Lord alone (mām eva prapadyante) cross over his guṇa-made māyā; the knower takes refuge after many births, knowing 'Vāsudeva is all'; taking refuge in him, people strive for release from old age and death; whoever takes refuge in him — even those of sinful birth, women, vaiśyas and śūdras — reaches the highest goal.

name: Singing the Lord's names (kīrtana, nāma-saṅkīrtana)
method_summary: BhG 9.14: the great souls worship the Lord always singing his praise (satataṃ kīrtayantaḥ), striving, firm in vows and bowing to him with devotion, ever yoked.

name: Bowing to the Lord (namaskāra)
method_summary: BhG 9.14, 9.34: bowing to the Lord with devotion as part of the great souls' worship; enjoined in the closing verse of ch. 9, 'bow to me' (māṃ namaskuru).

name: The sacrifice of knowledge (jñāna-yajña)
method_summary: BhG 9.15: some worship the Lord by the sacrifice of knowledge — as one, as separate, and in many ways, him whose faces are everywhere. The verse gives no further method.

name: Offering a leaf, flower, fruit or water with devotion
method_summary: BhG 9.26: whoever offers the Lord with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water — that devout offering of one pure/intent of self the Lord eats (accepts).

name: Offering all actions to the Lord (mad-arpaṇa)
method_summary: BhG 9.27–28 (with 8.7): whatever one does, eats, offers in the fire, gives or performs as austerity is to be done as an offering to the Lord; thus one is released from the bonds of action with their good and bad fruits and, with the self yoked in the yoga of renunciation, freed, comes to him; mind and intellect offered to him.
signs_of_progress: release from the bonds of action with auspicious and inauspicious fruits (9.28)
